declared: Storm shelter life support: 72 h for 10 people from the life-support room on the same deck (design provision, not computed).

Galactic cosmic rays: at 2026 free-space rates (1.8 mSv/day, ~657 mSv/yr) a crew member reaches NASA's 600 mSv career limit after ~333 days in deep space. Hull shielding barely changes this. Long careers aboard rely on canon's off-Earth MED-MOD-RADIATION milestone and crew time-in-space rules; this is a canon question, not something the hull can close.

Torch neutrons and gammas: the shadow shield must attenuate the torch's neutron and gamma output so the dose rate inside the habitat during burns stays within crew limits. The torch's source strength is canon and not modelled here; only the shadow geometry is checked.
notes: Shadow cone: shield front face x 34.3 m, radius 2.75 m; neutron source a 1.0 m plasma column anywhere in x 39.3-46.3 m (worst case used); radiator strakes outside the cone take neutron heating and are out of bounds for EVA during burns.
